data.one_liner: Provides smooth flying animations between widgets or screen coordinates.
data.what_it_does: FlyMotion lets you animate a widget from one position to another using GlobalKeys or explicit offsets. It renders the animation in an overlay with configurable duration, curvature, and repeat settings.
use_when: You need a visual “fly” effect between two UI elements, such as adding items to a cart
You want to animate objects based on touch coordinates or custom paths
avoid_when: You only need simple built‑in Flutter transitions (e.g., FadeTransition)
You require physics‑based or gesture‑driven animations beyond a fixed Bezier curve
strengths: Minimal API, easy to drop in
Supports both widget‑key and coordinate‑based launches
weaknesses: Relies on overlay_support as a hard dependency
Limited to quadratic Bezier curves, no physics simulation
No built‑in support for complex sequencing beyond repeatCount
data.setup_notes: Wrap the app with FlyMotionOverlaySupport as shown in the README

alternatives.name: flutter_animate
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers a broader set of declarative animation utilities without needing an overlay wrapper

alternatives.name: lottie
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides rich, pre‑designed animations and can be used for similar visual effects without custom code
